subject: bicycle
pitch: A vintage Dutch city bicycle in mint green. Tall upright handlebars with cream grips and a silver bell, a brown leather saddle with springs, chrome mudguards, a chain guard, a wicker basket on the front filled with sunflowers and a baguette, and whitewall tyres.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a bicycle model as a TypeScript module, using torus geometry for the wheels and tube/rod primitives for the frame, handlebars, saddle, mudguards, chain guard, and a basket with sunflowers and a baguette, all connected through a joint hierarchy.

For wheels I'm using dark torus geometry for the tyre with a thin whitewall ring offset on the sidewall, rotating the torus geometry so its axis aligns with the wheel's X axle instead of the default Z.

I'm adding a chrome rim cylinder, silver hub, and a dozen thin rod spokes per wheel connecting hub to rim for a classic look, keeping part counts reasonable.

Now I'm mapping out the frame geometry using rod sweeps: down tube, top tube, seat stays, chain stays, and a fork, connecting the bottom bracket, head tube, seat, and hubs with offset pairs for the rear stays.

Next I'm working out the handlebars -- an upright stem rising from the head tube, with a curved bar built from a catmull spline across grip points on either side.

For grips I'm adding short rods capped in cream at the bar ends, and for the saddle I'm shaping a scaled sphere geometry to approximate a brown leather seat.

Now I'm adding a seat post rod and small spring-like connectors beneath the saddle, then moving on to chrome mudguard arcs using torus geometry curved over each wheel.

Widening the mudguard band and setting it to a chrome tone, then sketching a simple box shape for the chain guard near the rear.

Now I'm placing the chainring as a flat dark-chrome cylinder near the bottom bracket, with a small mint box plate serving as the chain guard above it, then adding a silver dome bell on the handlebar.

For the basket, I'm planning a wicker-textured frustum shape mounted between the handlebars above the front wheel, possibly using an SVG woven pattern texture in tan for the basket material to give it a realistic look.

For the sunflowers, I'm scattering 5 stems from inside the basket topped with flattened sphere discs for the yellow petals and small brown spheres for the centers, using random positions for a natural arrangement. Now I'm thinking through how to shape a baguette, considering a swept capsule form in tan or brown tones.

I'm now positioning the basket on the front rack: figuring out where it sits between the handlebar and front wheel, deciding its mount via support rods, and sizing an open cylinder geometry (wider top, narrower bottom) for the basket shape itself.

For texturing, I'm planning a woven-wicker look using a simple SVG pattern with diagonal brown lines over a tan background, mapped onto the basket's cylinder UVs.

For the wheels, I'm setting up whitewall tyres as rotated toruses positioned at the front and rear hubs, and defining the joint hierarchy -- front, rear, head, and seat joints all parented to the main frame bone -- before moving into rod connections for the frame structure.

Now I'm working out the spoke geometry: for each wheel in the YZ plane, spokes radiate from the hub at small radial offsets to rim points around the circle, using thin tube-swept rods, with 16 spokes per wheel (32 total) plus roughly 10 frame rods, keeping part count reasonable. I'm also sizing a chrome rim torus to sit just inside the tyre's tube radius so it stays visible rather than fully hidden.

For the tyre and rim details, I'm settling on a torus with major radius ~0.31 and tube ~0.022 for the tyre, adding cream whitewall rings offset slightly along the axle so they bulge onto the sidewalls symmetrically on both sides, and placing a chrome rim torus at radius ~0.27 with a small tube to sit centered within the tyre's inner diameter.

I'm skipping that rim torus since it's hidden inside the tyre, extending spokes to meet the rim at radius 0.285 instead, and building the hub as a small chrome cylinder rotated to align along the axle. For the mudguard, I'm using a partial torus arc rotated so it's centered over the top of the wheel, working out the geometry transformations so the arc sits symmetrically and figuring out where its ends land in space.

Now I'm positioning the fork legs so they run from the head tube down through to the front hub, laying out the frame tubes as single rods along the centerline for the main triangle while using paired rods offset in x for the chain stays and seat stays, and placing the head tube and handlebar stem segments with their chrome and mint colors. I'm starting to plan the handlebar curve using a spline through defined points.

Then I work out a symmetric curve for the handlebars, add grip rods at the bar ends, place a small bell on the bars, and size and position the saddle using a scaled sphere for the seat shape, positioning it on the seat post relative to the seat tube top.

For the saddle springs, I decide on a few short angled rods beneath the seat as a simplified spring approximation rather than modeling true coils, attaching them near the seat post. Then I set up the chainring as a flattened dark cylinder near the bottom bracket and add a simple box-shaped chain guard above it, skipping detailed pedal cranks for simplicity.

Now I'm working out the front basket: an open-topped cone-like cylinder sitting above the mudguard and below the handlebars, supported by rods running from the fork crown down to its base, with a flat circular bottom rotated to face upward, textured to look wicker-like using the same material as the basket walls.

For the sunflowers, I'm placing five stems rising from inside the basket to head positions above, each flower head built as a flattened yellow sphere oriented outward-and-up via a direction vector, with a small brown flattened sphere offset along that same direction to form the center disc, and I'm considering adding a ring of petal shapes around each head for more detail.

For the baguette, I'm sweeping a tapered tube along a curved path lying diagonally across the top of the basket, using a radius function that thins toward both ends and rounded caps, in a warm bread-crust color, and I'm deciding to skip adding separate score-line details to keep things simple.

I'm laying out the bike's joint hierarchy next—root frame joint, then front and rear wheel hubs, head tube, and seat joint—so that wheels, basket, handlebars, and fork pieces can all attach to the right rigid bone. For the wheels I'm writing a reusable function that builds the tire as a rotated torus, adds whitewall stripes by translating duplicate thin tori sideways, places a chrome cylindrical hub, and then generates sixteen crossed spokes as thin rods connecting hub points to offset rim points around the circle.

I'm also sketching out the frame tubes, fork legs, chain stays, and seat stays as simple rods between key frame coordinates, plus basket support rods running from near the head joint down to the basket's outer edge, all attached to the appropriate bones. For the basket's woven texture, I'm generating an SVG pattern with diagonal crossing lines to simulate a wicker weave, accepting that it may not rasterize in a headless environment but will render correctly in a browser. Finally, I'm assembling all of this into a build function that creates the builder, adds every part and joint, and returns the root, alongside a small metadata export describing the model.
